text:
Emma: heads up — p99 memory for KV cache is climbing on long-context workloads. Seen after ~60k tokens, growth looks like lots of tiny allocations at the allocator fringe :eyes:

raj: can you paste the profiler snippet? which allocator are we using (bucketed vs buddy)?

Emma: using our small-block arena (32/64/128/256 bins). heap hist from profiler: 
```
TOTAL  1280MB
 arena_small_bin_32  280MB (21.9%)
 arena_small_bin_64  340MB (26.6%)
 arena_small_bin_128 210MB (16.4%)
 arena_frag_meta      120MB (9.4%)
 other                330MB (25.8%)
```
Looks like lots of fragmentation in 32/64 bins after long-context KV writes.

sasha: that matches what I saw in the stress harness — many tiny KV entries created by token-level caching when batching is high. Bin churn + freelist fragmentation.

taylor: do we have an allocation timeline? is it steady leak or plateauing at higher mem?

Emma: timeline is steady climb during generation, then small drops when eviction/paging runs, but not enough. Paging threshold kicks in at 75% mem and evicts ~20% entries yet fragmentation remains.

liam: curious — did the recent allocator change to avoid coalescing small holes (to speed alloc) land in the same release? Could be preventing multi-block merges.

raj: yep, that was the change. It reduced alloc latency by ~8% under microbench but may increase fragmentation. We traded latency for re-use.

perf-bot: benchmark/kv-longcontext v2: throughput -1.2%, p99 latency +3.5% when coalescing enabled; throughput -0.6% when disabled but memory usage +12% on long traces.

sasha: tradeoff is visible. We need an approach that keeps alloc latency but reduces long-run fragmentation. Ideas: slightly larger minimal block (64->128), deferred/partial coalescing (background thread), or occasional compaction pass during low load.

taylor: partial/background compaction seems promising — avoid stop-the-world. Do we have locking concerns for background merges?

liam: background worker can coordinate via lock-free freelist handoff or per-thread arenas with periodic global consolidation. Key is doing small bounded work slices to avoid hiccups.

raj: also consider tuning batching heuristics — larger batches mean more contiguous KV writes which may help fill blocks sequentially and reduce holes. But that affects latency SLOs.

Emma: agreed. Proposed experiment plan:
1) run long-context perf with min-block 64 vs 128 vs 256
2) enable incremental background coalesce that runs X ms every Y s (configurable)
3) run with batch-size cap at 8 vs 16 to see fragmentation sensitivity
Collect: peak mem, p50/p99 latency, throughput, and compaction CPU.

sasha: I can wire up the harness to sweep those three axes.

raj: add one more variant: keep min-block 64 but enable lightweight meta-compression (store adjacent tiny entries in a slab inline) — low-risk software change.

liam: note: earlier full-compaction prototype reduced resident set but regressed throughput by ~8% because it paused allocation for >50ms spikes. Avoid that.

Emma: yep we want no >5ms tail. Background bounded passes only. Also add metrics: free-list fragmentation ratio and avg contiguous-run-length so we can correlate.

perf-bot: scheduled: kv-longcontext sweep job queued (ETA ~2h).

raj: thanks — once we have results, we can decide whether to revert alloc change or ship background coalesce by default. :thumbsup:

Emma: thanks all — priority: reduce long-run mem growth without hurting p99 latency. Will post results in this thread.
